claimText: Tesla cars can drive themselves fully autonomously without any human intervention

brave.title: Tesla Autopilot and FSD: What can Tesla cars actually do?
brave.description: Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving (FSD) capabilities require active driver supervision. Tesla states drivers must keep hands on the wheel and be ready to take over at any time.

brave.title: NHTSA: Tesla's FSD requires human supervision
brave.description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration classifies Tesla's FSD as a Level 2 driver-assistance system, meaning human supervision is required at all times.

brave.title: Reuters: Tesla faces scrutiny over 'Full Self-Driving' marketing claims
brave.description: Tesla's FSD beta requires drivers to remain attentive. Despite the name, it does not provide full autonomous driving capability. Multiple crashes have occurred during Autopilot use.

brave.title: The Verge: Tesla's Full Self-Driving — what it is and what it isn't
brave.description: Tesla's FSD is an advanced driver-assistance feature, not true autonomous driving. The SAE classifies it as Level 2, meaning the driver must always be ready to intervene.

brave.title: Consumer Reports: Tesla Autopilot review and safety concerns
brave.description: Consumer Reports found Tesla's Autopilot and FSD perform well in many scenarios but emphasize these are driver-assistance features, not full self-driving technology.

factCheck.text: Tesla cars can drive fully autonomously

claimReviewMarkup.title: Mostly False: Tesla FSD requires human supervision
